sc: Well 5-year-old with fever, soft musical systolic murmur that changes with posture → Still's murmur: reassure
Well newborn, sudden cyanosis or shock on day 2–5 → Duct closing: start PGE1
Mother with lupus, newborn heart rate 50 → Congenital complete heart block
f: 3 shunts: ductus venosus, foramen ovale, ductus arteriosus · duct closes functionally in 1–3 days (PGE1 keeps it open, ibuprofen closes it)
Soft, systolic, short, changes with posture · normal S2, no thrill, well child · venous hum disappears lying down
Diastolic, pansystolic, loud (≥ 3/6), thrill · abnormal S2 · symptoms (poor feeding, sweating, cyanosis)
Wide fixed split S2 = ASD · single S2 = TOF, TGA · radio-femoral delay = coarctation · collapsing pulse = PDA/AR
Echocardiography (best) · ECG · chest X-ray (boot heart = TOF, egg-on-side = TGA) · SpO2 screen < 95% → echo
Commonest CHD: VSD · cyanotic at birth: TGA · cyanotic after infancy: TOF · Down syndrome: AVSD
trap: Cyanotic infants are often not distressed in proportion (TOF); breathless infants with plethoric lungs have a left-to-right shunt · a murmur in a febrile child: re-examine when afebrile
